result:
No more questions. One thing before I write it up: how it gets built. You've talked about outcomes and left the build to me, so here are the options and my choice.

**1. Add it to the taproom app (my pick).** Batch tracking goes into the Flask app already running on the office Pi, with new tables in the same SQLite database. Brewers would use a simple scan page on a phone or tablet, with a cheap barcode scanner, to:
- start a batch
- scan each sack's lot number as it's opened
- record bottling, which sends the batch number and date to the label printer

This has the fewest moving parts: one machine, one app, and one backup to look after. The cost is that a bug in the new code could, in principle, affect running tabs. I'd keep the batch code in its own section of the app to limit that.

**2. A separate small app on the same Pi.** This keeps tabs completely apart from batch records, but it means two apps to start, update and back up. It only pays off if you expect the tracking to grow well beyond what we've discussed.

**3. Off-the-shelf brewery software.** I've dropped this one. Most of it is subscription-based and cloud-hosted, and most expects lot numbers to be typed in. That's the opposite of the wet-hands, scan-it workflow you described, and you'd be fitting your process to theirs.

I'll go with option 1 unless you stop me. This counts as a project rather than a small change, so my next message will be the full written design, saved in the repo under `specs/`. A reviewer will read it first, and I may come back once with a few questions. After that it's yours to review.
